title: Task list and progress components
goal: Provide small, reusable task-list and progress components so any lane can show what an agent plans to do and how far a long operation has got.
scope_in: `<TaskList items maxRows />` for agent plan/todo items: glyphs `○` pending, `◐` in progress, `✓` done (ASCII `[ ]`, `[~]`, `[x]` without unicode), done items dimmed, in-progress item in `text.primary` bold; header `Tasks 3/7`.

Collapsing: show at most `maxRows` (default 10) with the in-progress item always visible and a final row `⋯ +4 more`; toggled by action `tasks.toggle` (`ctrl+t`) as a panel above the prompt, remembered per session.

`<ProgressBar>` determinate `▕████████░░░░▏ 62 %` using `█` and `░` (coloured `signal` on `border.subtle`), width-adaptive (min 10 cells, label never truncated before the bar), always with a label of what is progressing.
Indeterminate bar: sliding 6-cell block `▏░░▓▓▓░░░░▕` advancing one cell every 80 ms; in reduced motion it is a static bar with the label plus `…`.
`useProgress` helper exposing `{value, label}` from bus events of the form `{type:'progress', id, value, total?, label}`.
Task update intake: `reduceTasks(state, update)` for a `TaskUpdate = {tasks: {id, text, status}[]}` supplied by the agent runner (replace-all semantics, order preserved).
scope_out: Emitting task updates from the agent (lane C013 / C014 wiring).
build_against: Pure component tests with prop fixtures and the pty/TUI snapshot tester from lane C008 (ink-testing-library plus pty harness, frames captured at 80x24 and 120x40). No backend is needed; any session data comes from contracts/fixtures/events/*.json or hand-built typed values from @centcom/protocol (lane C003).
interfaces: `<TaskList items: TaskItem[]; maxRows?: number; width: number; title?: string />`; `type TaskItem = {id: string; text: string; status: 'pending'|'in_progress'|'completed'}`
`<ProgressBar value?: number /*0..1, undefined = indeterminate*/; label: string; width: number; motion?: 'full'|'reduced' />`
`reduceTasks(state: TaskState, update: TaskUpdate): TaskState`; `useProgress(bus: EventBus, id: string): {value?: number; label: string}`
`renderBar(value: number, cells: number): string` pure function
acceptance: `renderBar(0.62, 12)` returns 7 filled cells (7.44 rounded) so the full determinate line equals `▕███████░░░░░▏ 62 %`; 0 and 1 render all empty / all filled with `0 %` and `100 %`.
Indeterminate: over 10 ticks of 80 ms the 6-cell block moves one cell each tick and bounces at both ends; the string width is constant at 12 cells.

With 12 tasks and `maxRows=10` where task 11 is in progress, the in-progress task is visible and the list ends with `⋯ +N more` where N is the number hidden; list never exceeds `maxRows + 2` rows including header and footer.
Task text longer than the width is truncated with `…`; it is never wrapped onto a second row.
Under `NO_COLOR` and `unicode:false` the list uses `[ ] [~] [x]` and the bar uses `#` and `-` with brackets `[##########----] 62 %`.
Status unknown (`status:'blocked'`) renders as pending and does not throw.
`ProgressBar` without a label is a TypeScript compile error and a runtime dev warning; value outside 0..1 is clamped.
Unmounting clears the 80 ms timer (leak test).
tests: tasks/bar.test.ts: renderBar table incl. rounding and clamping.
tasks/indeterminate.test.ts: fake timers, bounce, reduced motion.
tasks/list.test.ts: collapse rules, truncation, glyph fallbacks.
guardrails: MUST always render a label with a progress bar (DESIGN §10.1.7).
MUST NOT convey status by colour only; glyph and dim/bold differences are required.
MUST sanitise task text (it comes from model output) before rendering.
MUST cap items at 200 and update batching at one render per 80 ms.
MUST NOT animate in reduced-motion or non-TTY output.
failure_modes: `total` of 0 in progress events -> treat as indeterminate.
Task update with duplicate ids -> keep the last, log at debug.
notes: Task data source (todo tool events) is not defined by the contracts because the local agent's todo state is not a wire event; wiring is a runner concern. If tasks must be shared across members later, that needs a contract change.
